intent: To demonstrate that Trump supporters' confidence in the accuracy of vote counting increased significantly after his 2016 election victory.

requirements.question: Is the within-group Aug-to-Nov increase in 'Very' required, or is showing only the higher Nov 'Very' value sufficient?

units.claim: The 'Very' confidence relative value for the group corresponding to Trump supporters (the group with the lower Aug 2016 'Very' value) increases substantially from Aug 2016 to Nov 2016: 0.0764 to 0.3264, roughly 4.3 times its earlier relative value.

basis.note: Lower of the two Aug 2016 'Very' values; this is the rising group per intent.
Higher of the two Nov 2016 'Very' values; same group as the Aug 0.0764 value.

accept: The 'Very' relative value for the rising group jumps from 0.0764 in Aug 2016 to 0.3264 in Nov 2016.
Trump-support 'Very' confidence rises from a very low relative value to its highest Nov value.
The group with the lower Aug 'Very' value increases its 'Very' relative value roughly fourfold by Nov.
units.evidence: The chart must show the same group's 'Very' relative value at both Aug 2016 and Nov 2016, with the Nov value clearly greater than the Aug value.

g0_data_completeness.selection: all role=bar data rows; annotation rows excluded

clip_hardcase.reason: The reference SVG has no explicit data-role=bar mark, so visual-unit reconstruction needs manual review.

hardcases.handling: Requires human visual inspection before semantic scoring.
